captions: Let's break down the Ardee Industries I-P-O —
a four hundred and twenty-six crore issue from a battery-recycling company,
and the fastest-growing business of this whole batch.
We'll cover what it does, its financials,
where the money goes,
and how much you'd need to apply as a retail or an H-N-I investor.
This is education, not investment advice.
So what does Ardee Industries do?
It's a recycling company.
It takes end-of-life batteries and other energy-storage products and recovers the lead and non-ferrous metals inside them.
It then refines that into high-purity lead and specialised alloys,
which it sells to battery makers,
the e-mobility and automotive industries,
and chemical companies.
It's based in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh,
and it sits on a genuinely interesting theme —
the circular economy.
As batteries and E-Vs grow, so does the need to recycle them.
Now the financials —
and they're the strongest growth story of this batch.
Revenue jumped fifty-seven percent,
from about seven hundred and forty-three crore to over eleven hundred and sixty-seven crore in FY twenty twenty-six.
And net profit exploded a hundred and fifty-five percent,
from thirty-three crore to nearly eighty-five crore.
That's genuinely rapid growth.
The grey market has taken notice too,
pricing a premium of around twenty-four percent —
but remember, that number is unofficial and drifts every day.
Where does your money go?
Here Ardee strikes a healthy balance.
Of the four hundred and twenty-six crore issue,
three hundred and twenty crore — about seventy-five percent —
is a fresh issue, money going into the company.
The remaining one hundred and six crore is an offer for sale,
where the promoters, Sandeep and Nikunj Aggarwal,
sell part of their stake and take some cash off the table.
So this isn't a pure sell-down like some I-P-Os,
nor entirely fresh — three-quarters funds the business,
one-quarter rewards the founders.
A reasonable, common structure.
What does the fresh money fund?
The large majority — about two hundred and twenty crore —
goes into working capital.
That makes sense: a recycling and metals business ties up a lot of cash in inventory and raw material,
so growth needs funding.
Around twenty crore repays debt, cutting interest costs,
and the rest is for general purposes.
The flip side to watch — a working-capital-heavy,
commodity-linked model means both cash needs and profits can swing with lead prices.
Should you subscribe?
The strengths are attractive — it's growing explosively,
with revenue up fifty-seven percent and profit up a hundred and fifty-five; three-quarters of the issue is fresh money funding the business; and it rides the E-V and battery-recycling theme,
which the grey market clearly likes.
The watch-outs —
its profits are tied to volatile lead and commodity prices; the model is working-capital hungry,
so it always needs cash; and a quarter of the issue is the promoters cashing out.
The takeaway — the best growth and structure of this batch,
but a commodity-linked business.
Understand the lead-price risk before you decide.
Finally — how do you apply, and how much do you need?
Retail investors can bid up to two lakh rupees for a thirty-five percent quota,
with allotment by lottery if it's oversubscribed —
so a bigger cheque doesn't help.
H-N-Is bid above two lakh for a fifteen percent quota.
For Ardee, one lot is two hundred and eighty-one shares —
about fourteen thousand eight hundred and ninety-three rupees —
your minimum.
Track the live subscription on the N-S-E and B-S-E I-P-O pages,
Chittorgarh, Moneycontrol, or your broker app.
Let's recap Ardee Industries.
A battery and lead-recycling business on the circular-economy theme,
and the fastest grower of this batch —
revenue up fifty-seven percent,
profit up a hundred and fifty-five.
The issue is a healthy mix: seventy-five percent fresh money funding the company,
twenty-five percent a promoter sell-down,
with the fresh money mainly funding working capital.
Retail minimum is about fourteen thousand eight hundred and ninety-three rupees,
and the grey-market premium is around twenty-four percent,
though that's unofficial.
This video explains the IPO for education only —
it is not investment advice,
not a buy or sell recommendation,
and not a prediction of listing gains.
Grey-market premium is unofficial and changes hourly.
Always read the RHP and check the live subscription before you apply.
Thanks for watching.
